subject: gk
question: What is the role of the Foreigners' Tribunal in the NRC (National Register of Citizens) process?

options.text: To verify citizenship claims of individuals excluded from the NRC

solution:
The correct answer is __**To verify citizenship claims of individuals excluded from the NRC**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Foreigners' Tribunal (FT) is a quasi-judicial body in India tasked with determining the **citizenship status** of individuals excluded from the NRC.
 
• It assesses cases where individuals are suspected or alleged to be illegal immigrants, particularly in the state of Assam, under the provisions of the **Foreigners Act, 1946**.
 
• The tribunal provides an opportunity for individuals to present evidence and prove their citizenship as per the guidelines of the NRC.
 
• It plays a critical role in ensuring that no genuine Indian citizen is wrongfully excluded from the NRC, while illegal immigrants are identified.
 
• The tribunals operate under the supervision of the Ministry of Home Affairs and consist of lawyers or retired judicial officers as members.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Register of Citizens (NRC):**

 
 
• The NRC is a register containing the names of all genuine Indian citizens in a specific region, primarily implemented in Assam to identify illegal immigrants.
 
• The first NRC was prepared in 1951 following the Census of 1951.
 
• The NRC process is governed by the Citizenship Act, 1955, and its associated rules.
 
 
 
• **Foreigners Act, 1946:**
 
 
• This act empowers the government to detect, detain, and deport illegal immigrants residing in the country.
 
• Under this act, the burden of proving citizenship lies with the individual whose status is under question.
 
 
 
• **Illegal Immigrants:**
 
 
• An illegal immigrant is a person who enters or resides in a country without proper legal authorization.
 
• In the context of the NRC, this includes individuals who entered India after the cut-off date of March 24, 1971, without valid documentation.
 
 
 
• **Quasi-Judicial Bodies:**
 
 
• These are institutions that have powers resembling judicial functions but are not part of the judiciary.
 
• The Foreigners' Tribunal is an example of a quasi-judicial body, as it makes determinations on citizenship status.
 
 
 
• **Assam Accord (1985):**
 
 
• It was an agreement signed between the Government of India and the leaders of the Assam Movement to address the issue of illegal immigration.
 
• The cut-off date for inclusion in the NRC was set as March 24, 1971, under this accord.
